To serve, divide the cauliflower mash, carrots, and pork chops between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Sautéed Kale & Sweet Potato Mash

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut out and discard the stems from the kale leaves; chop the leaves into 1-inch pieces and transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 1-inch cubes; transfer to a small saucepan. Cover the potatoes with hot water (from the tap) by about 1 inch; bring to a boil over high heat.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they develop a nice crust, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and cook the chops, flipping occasionally, until they are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife), another 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer the pork to a plate.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce the heat to medium-high and boil the potatoes until they can be easily pierced with a fork, 8 to 10 minutes. Scoop out ½ cup of the cooking water and drain the rest. Cover the potatoes to keep warm.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.

Once the pork has been transferred, add the garlic, crushed red pepper, kale, and ½ cup water to the skillet; toss to combine. Cover with a lid and cook until the kale is wilted but still green, 4 to 6 minutes. Remove the cover and continue to cook, stirring, until all of the liquid has evaporated, another 1 to 2 minutes.
Remove the kale from the heat, then drizzle with apple cider vinegar and season with salt and pepper, toss to combine.
Add ½ of the reserved liquid, butter, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher until smooth. Add more of the liquid to thin out the mash if needed.
To serve, divide the sweet potato mash, sautéed kale, and pork chops between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Sautéed Spinach & Parsnip-Apple Purée

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel the parsnips, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Large dice the parsnips (cut into ¾-inch cubes) and transfer to a large bowl.
Quarter the apple lengthwise, then cut out the core and stem from each section; large dice the apple (cut into ¾-inch cubes) and add to the bowl with the parsnips.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan heats up, peel and mince or press the garlic; transfer to a small bowl.
Add butter to the saucepan, followed by the chopped parsnips, apples, and ½ of the garlic (save the rest for the spinach). Sauté the parsnips and apples for 3 to 4 minutes.

Pour the broth into the saucepan and add an additional ¼ cup of water; increase the heat and bring the liquid to a boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat to a simmer, cover the saucepan with a lid, and cook the parsnips and apples until they are tender, about 10 minutes. Once done, remove the saucepan from the heat.
amounts: 4 fl oz (½ cup) chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they develop a nice crust, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and cook the chops, flipping occasionally, until they are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife), another 2 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer the pork to a plate.
Once the pork has been transferred, add the remaining garlic to the skillet; cook until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the spinach to the skillet and season with salt and pepper; cook, tossing, until the spinach has wilted, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to the parsnip-apple mixture and mash with a hand blender or potato masher until smooth.
To serve, spoon the parsnip-apple purée onto a plate and top with the sautéed spinach and a pork chop. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Warm Asparagus-Potato Salad

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Halve the potatoes lengthwise, then place in a small saucepan and cover with hot water (from the tap); bring to a boil. Once boiling, cook until the potatoes are tender (but not falling apart) when pierced with a knife, 12 to 18 minutes. Once done, take the potatoes out of the saucepan with a spoon and place on a plate.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; cut the spears into 1-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to a medium bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they develop a nice crust, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and cook the chops, flipping occasionally, until they are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife), another 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer the pork to a plate.
While the pork chops cook, juice the lemon into a large salad bowl, then add yogurt, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together.

Once the pork chops have been transferred, add the asparagus to the skillet. Cook, tossing frequently, until the asparagus is bright green and just tender, 4 to 6 minutes, lowering the heat if needed to keep it from burning. Once done, add to the salad bowl.
While the asparagus cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle and add to the salad bowl.
Transfer the cooked potatoes to the cutting board. Halve each half lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch-thick pieces. Add to the salad bowl.
Toss the salad until it is thoroughly coated in the dressing.
To serve, divide the pork chops and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Yogurt Sauce & Tomato-Cucumber Salad

instructions.text: In a small bowl, prepare the yogurt sauce by whisking together the yogurt, vinegar, olive oil, dill, salt, and pepper. Place in the fridge to chill.
amounts: ½ tsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Season both sides of the pork chops with salt and pepper.
Add oil to the skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add the pork chops and cook until browned and cooked through, 3-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and let them rest for 2-3 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. Halve the cucumber crosswise, then quarter lengthwise and slice crosswise on an angle; transfer to a medium bowl. Halve the tomatoes; add to the bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; add to bowl with salad. Drizzle the salad with olive oil and season with oregano, salt, and pepper; toss to coat.
To serve, arrange the tomato-cucumber salad on a plate and place a pork chops over top. Spoon yogurt sauce on top of the pork or serve on the side and enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Sausage & Warm Broccoli Caesar with Crispy Bread Crumbs

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Wash, dry, and separate broccoli into bite-sized florets; cut stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with salt; toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until broccoli is golden brown and tender, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bread crumbs and salt; cook, stirring frequently, until golden and crispy, 3-5 minutes. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside to cool. (Reserve skillet for next step.)

Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels. Return to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausages and cook, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 12-15 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Transfer to another small bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Mince anchovy fillet. Add both to the bowl with the Parmesan.
Wash, dry, and juice lemon into the bowl. Add mayo, oil, pepper, and salt; whisk to combine the dressing.
To serve, divide sausages and broccoli between plates. Drizzle broccoli with dressing and top with crispy bread crumbs. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Salmon with Carrot, Beet & Apple Slaw

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the apple, then cut out the core and stem from each section; using a box grater, coarsely grate the sections and transfer to a large salad bowl.
Peel the carrot, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Coarsely grate the carrot and add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the beet; peel and coarsely grate the beet. (To avoid staining, line your cutting board with paper towels before handling the beet.) Add the beet to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to the salad bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the salmon dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
When the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the salmon, skin-side down, in the skillet; cook the salmon until it is cooked through and flaky, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Once done, remove the skillet from the heat.
While the salmon cooks, roughly chop the walnuts and add to the salad bowl.
Juice the lemon and add to the salad bowl.
Add olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper to the salad bowl; mix the ingredients until well combined.
To serve, spoon the carrot, beet and apple slaw onto a plate and place the salmon over top. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Salmon with Cauliflower & Spinach Power Mash

instructions.text: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stems; roughly cut into bite-sized florets.
Once the water is boiling, add the cauliflower and cook until fork-tender, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and medium dice the onion.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic.
Add garlic to the skillet with the onion; cook, stirring constantly, 1 minute more. Remove from heat and transfer the garlic and onion to a blender.
Pick basil leaves off the stems; add leaves to the blender along with cream, butter, salt, and pepper.

Place the spinach in a large colander in the sink. When the cauliflower is cooked, carefully empty into the colander to drain; add cauliflower and wilted spinach to the blender. Blend on high, until smooth, about 1 minute. Set aside.
Pat salmon dry with paper towels and cut into fillets; season with salt and pepper.
Wipe out skillet and return to heat; add more butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add salmon to the skillet, skin-side down, and reduce heat to medium. Cook 4 minutes and then flip, cooking an additional 3-4 minutes, until the fish is firm and cooked through.
Cut lemon into wedges.
To serve, divide spinach mash between plates and top with butter; place salmon on the side and garnish with lemon wedges. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Salmon with Creamy Green Beans

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Trim and discard the ends of the green beans, then halve the green beans and transfer to a medium bowl.
Juice the lemon into a large salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the lemon juice.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add the green beans. Cook until bright green and tender-crisp, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, drain in a colander and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking process. Set aside to drain further.
To the lemon juice and garlic, add yogurt, olive oil, salt, and pepper; whisk together.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the salmon dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Carefully place the salmon, skin-side-down, in the skillet; cook until the flesh is opaque and flaky, 3 to 4 minutes per side (depending on thickness). Once done, transfer the salmon to a plate.
Add the green beans to the salad bowl and toss to thoroughly coat in the dressing.
To serve, divide the green beans and salmon between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Salmon with Mango Salsa, Sautéed Asparagus & Jasmine Rice

instructions.text: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince shallot; place in a small bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the shallot.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Small dice and add to the bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl, then add oil and spices. Stir to combine the mango salsa and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the salmon dry with paper towels and place, skin-side down, on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on the top-side.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add salmon, skin-side down, and cook, flipping once, until skin is crispy and flesh is opaque, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus; cut spears into 2-inch pieces.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add asparagus and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice, salmon, and asparagus between plates. Top salmon with salsa and enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Sausage with Cheesy Brussels Sprouts & Broccoli

instructions.text: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add sausages and cook, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 12-15 minutes. Transfer sausages to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
While the sausages are cooking, fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and trim Brussels sprouts.
Once the water in the pan is boiling, uncover, add salt and Brussels sprouts, and stir for a few seconds. Reduce heat to medium and cook until starting to soften, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry broccoli; separate into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces.

Once the Brussels sprouts start to soften, add broccoli and continue to cook until veggies are fork-tender, 5-6 minutes more. Drain veggies and transfer to a medium bowl; set aside. (Reserve pan for later use.)
While the veggies are cooking, coarsely grate cheese and set aside.
Return pan to medium heat. Once the pan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add flour and whisk until smooth. Cook, whisking frequently, until lightly golden, 1 minute.
Slowly pour milk into the pan, whisking constantly. Continue whisking until the sauce has thickened, 3-4 minutes.
amounts: 10 fl oz (1 ¼ cups) whole milk

instructions.text: Add cheese and spices to the pan; whisk until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth.
Return drained veggies to the pan with the sauce and stir to combine. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide sausages and cheesy veggies between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Sausage with Fennel, Apple, Celery, Walnut & Parmesan Salad

instructions.text: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, roughly chop walnuts.
Once the skillet is hot, add walnuts and cook, stirring frequently, until lightly toasted, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a small bowl. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)
Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausages and cook, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 12-15 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulb. Halve fennel bulb lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice celery. Add to the bowl.
Quarter, core, and thinly slice apple. Add to the bowl.
Pick parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems. Add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
Using a peeler, shave Parmesan into curls.
To serve, divide sausages and salad between plates; top salad with walnuts and Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Sole with Mashed Potatoes & Green Beans

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel the potatoes, then halve lengthwise and crosswise; transfer the quarters to a small saucepan. Cover with hot water (from the tap) by about 1 inch and bring to a boil over high heat.
Trim and discard the ends of the green beans, then halve the green beans. Transfer to a medium bowl.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce the heat to medium and cook until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife, 8 to 12 minutes. Once done, reserve about ½ cup of liquid and drain the rest. Cover the saucepan to keep warm.
Add butter to a nonstick skillet and preheat over medium heat.
Pat the sole dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add the sole; cook until it is cooked through and golden brown, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Once the sole has been transferred, add the green beans to the skillet and pour in ¼ cup of water. Bring to a boil over high heat; once boiling, cook until bright green, 2 to 3 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Add the garlic, butter, salt, and pepper to the green beans. Cook until the water is fully evaporated, another 1 to 2 minutes.
Add ½ of the reserved liquid, butter, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher until smooth. Add more liquid to thin out the mash if needed.
To serve, divide the mashed potatoes, green beans, and sole between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Steak with Sautéed Kale & Sweet Potato Mash

ingredients.name: striploin (new york strip) steak
ingredients.display: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut out and discard the stems from the kale leaves; chop the leaves crosswise into 1-inch strips and transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 1-inch cubes; transfer to a small saucepan. Cover the potatoes with hot water (from the tap) by about 1 inch; bring to a boil over high heat.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
amounts: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate, leaving any juices in the skillet, and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce the heat to medium-high and boil the potatoes until they can be easily pierced with a fork, 8 to 10 minutes. Scoop out ½ cup of the cooking water and drain the rest. Cover the potatoes to keep warm.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.

Once the steak has been transferred, reduce the heat to medium and add more coconut oil. Add the garlic, crushed red pepper, kale, and ¼ cup water to the skillet; toss to combine. Cover with a lid and cook until the kale is wilted but still green, 4 to 6 minutes. Remove the cover and continue to cook, stirring, until all of the liquid has evaporated, another 1 to 2 minutes.
Drizzle the kale with apple cider vinegar and season with salt and pepper, toss to combine.
Add ½ of the reserved liquid, butter, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher until smooth. Add more of the liquid to thin out the mash if needed.
To serve, divide the sweet potato mash, sautéed kale, and steak between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Steak with Sweet Potato Mash & Green Beans

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 1-inch cubes; transfer to a small saucepan.
Add water to the saucepan, covering the potatoes, and bring to a boil. Cook until they are tender when pierced with a fork, 8 to 10 minutes.
Trim and discard the ends of the green beans; transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.

Once the steak has been transferred, add the green beans to the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook, tossing frequently, until they are bright green and tender-crisp, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, remove the skillet from the heat.
Once the potatoes are tender, scoop out ¼ cup of the water and set aside, then drain the potatoes in a colander and return them back to the saucepan.
Add the reserved cooking water, minced garlic, butter, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher (or a fork) until smooth.
To serve, divide the steak, sweet potato mash, and green beans between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Striploin Steak with Cauliflower & Leek Mash

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 6 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

ingredients.name: striploin (new york strip) steak
ingredients.display: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Wash cauliflower and cut off the leaves. Separate into small florets and cut the thick stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to medium saucepan.
Add broth to the saucepan, cover, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook until cauliflower is tender and easy to mash, about 12 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
amounts: 6 fl oz (¾ cup) chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Chop the bacon into small pieces. Add to the skillet and cook until crispy, 4-6 minutes. Once cooked, remove bacon bits from skillet with slotted spoon and drain on paper towel, leaving the drippings in the pan.

Trim off the root ends and the dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut the leek in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice on the diagonal into ¼ inch thick pieces.
Once the bacon has been transferred, add the leeks to the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 5 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Once the cauliflower is ready, mash with a fork or potato masher, adding the leeks, butter, and parsley to the saucepan.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
amounts: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
To serve, divide the cauliflower mash and steak between plates. Top the cauliflower with bacon bits. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Striploin Steak with Kale, Avocado & Grapefruit Salad

ingredients.name: striploin (new york strip) steak
ingredients.display: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut out and discard the kale stems; cut the leaves into 1-inch pieces. Transfer to a medium salad bowl.

Drizzle the kale with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Massage the kale with your hands until the leaves are evenly coated with the oil and begin to become more tender, 1 to 2 minutes. Set aside.
amounts: 1 ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
amounts: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Scoop out and large dice the avocado flesh into ¾-inch cubes; add to the salad bowl with the kale.

Slice off a piece from both grapefruit ends, then place it flat on one of the ends and slice off the peel (from top to bottom), exposing the flesh; cut out the segments of flesh from between the membranes, then cut them into ¾-inch pieces. Add the pieces (and any leftover juice) to the salad bowl.
Toss the salad until well combined.
Slice the steak against the grain into strips.
To serve, divide the salad and steak between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Tilapia with Couscous & Orange Avocado Salad

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, bring broth and spices to a boil. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork right before serving.
amounts: 8 fl oz (1 cup) chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest orange into a medium bowl, then add oil, vinegar, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing. (Reserve orange for the next step.)
Cut off skin and white pith from the orange; slice between the membranes to release segments. Cut each segment crosswise into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim, seed, and halve bell pepper crosswise, then slice into thin strips; add to the bowl.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat tilapia dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with spices on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tilapia and cook, flipping once, until fish is crispy and easily flakes with a fork, about 6 minutes; remove from heat.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; add to the bowl with orange and bell pepper.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and small dice the flesh. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide couscous, tilapia, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Tilapia with Potato, Snap Pea & Mint Salad

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the potato lengthwise (into wedges) and transfer to a small saucepan. Cover with hot water (from the tap) by about 1 inch and bring to a boil over high heat.
Grate the zest from the lemon, then juice the lemon; add both to a large bowl (that will hold the salad).
To the salad bowl, add yogurt, olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, cook the potato pieces until they are tender when pierced with a knife or fork, 10 to 15 minutes, making sure not to overcook. Drain in a colander.
Halve the sugar snap peas at an angle; add to the salad bowl.
Pick the mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and finely dice the shallot. Add to the salad bowl.
Add olive oil to a nonstick skillet and preheat over medium heat.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add the tilapia; cook until it is cooked through and golden brown, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Cut the potato quarters crosswise into ¼-inch-thick pieces; add to the salad bowl. Gently toss the salad until well coated with the dressing.
To serve, divide the tilapia and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Tilapia with Quinoa, Cucumber & Feta Salad

ingredients.name: crumbled feta cheese
ingredients.display: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine the quinoa and water; bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Add olive oil to a nonstick skillet and heat over medium heat.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the quinoa for 15 minutes. Once done, remove the quinoa from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with paprika, salt, and pepper on both sides.
Place the fish in the skillet; cook until opaque throughout, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
While the fish cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the cucumber; quarter the cucumber lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch-thick pieces. Transfer to a large salad bowl.
Cut off and discard the large stems from the dill; chop the dill leaves and tender stems. Add to the salad bowl.
Add the feta to the salad bowl.
amounts: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese.

instructions.text: Juice the lemon and add to the salad bowl.
Add olive oil, salt, and pepper to the salad bowl.
Uncover the quinoa and fluff with a fork; add to the salad bowl and toss to combine.
To serve, divide the quinoa between plates and top with the fish. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Cranberry & Pistachio Quinoa Salad

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.display: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine the quinoa and broth; bring to a boil over high heat.
amounts: 8 fl oz (1 cup) chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Roughly chop the pistachios and transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the quinoa for 15 minutes. Once done, remove the quinoa from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Season the cutlets with salt and pepper on both sides.
amounts: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless

instructions.text: Add the pistachios to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until the nuts are toasted and fragrant, 3 to 5 minutes. Return to the small bowl and wipe out the pan.
Once the pistachios have been transferred, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Place the chicken cutlets in the skillet; cook until they are golden brown on the outside and cooked through in the center, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm. Cook in batches if necessary.
Uncover the quinoa and fluff with a fork.

Once the chicken has been transferred, add olive oil to the skillet followed by the garlic, spinach, cooked quinoa, pistachios, and cranberries. Season with salt and pepper and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from the heat.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: To serve, divide the quinoa salad and chicken between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Zucchini Noodles & Creamy Lemon-Dill Spinach

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.display: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Trim zucchini and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles; transfer to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. Cut butter into small pieces and sprinkle over top; season with salt.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated), and roast, tossing halfway through, until zucchini is tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
amounts: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless

instructions.text: Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken to a plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, roughly chop spinach; place in a small bowl.
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the spinach and set aside.
Peel and mince garlic.
Return skillet to medium heat, add more butter, and swirl to coat the bottom; add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add broth and cream to the skillet; stir to combine the sauce and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until thickened, 6-7 minutes.
amounts: 8 fl oz (1 cup) chicken or vegetable broth
4 fl oz (½ cup) heavy whipping cream

instructions.text: Once the sauce has thickened, add spinach and dill in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Juice lemon into the skillet and stir to combine. Remove from heat.
Thinly slice chicken into strips.
To serve, divide zucchini noodles, spinach, and chicken between plates. Spoon sauce over chicken and enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Halibut with Citrus Butter Sauce & Parmesan-Asparagus

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus. Place on a baking sheet, drizzle with oil, and season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine.
Place asparagus in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until tender, 12-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the halibut dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add halibut and pan-fry, turning once, until lightly browned and just cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
Peel and mince shallot and garlic.
Juice lemon and orange into a small bowl.
Remove asparagus from the oven and sprinkle with half of the Parmesan. Return to the oven and bake until cheese is melted and golden, 2-3 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Transfer the cooked halibut to a clean plate and cover with foil. Return skillet to medium heat.
Add shallot and garlic to the skillet and cook, stirring frequently, until starting to soften, about 1 minute.
Add citrus juice and butter to the skillet, scraping up any browned bits. Cook, stirring frequently, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3 minutes.
To serve, divide asparagus, halibut, and citrus sauce between plates. Top with remaining Parmesan and enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Lamb Chops with Greek Salad & Avocado Dressing

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the root end of the lettuce and remove any blemished leaves; halve the lettuce lengthwise, then chop crosswise into 1-inch pieces and transfer to a large salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the cucumber; slice the cucumber crosswise into ⅛-inch-thick rounds and add to the salad bowl.
Halve the tomatoes and add to the salad bowl.
Halve the olives lengthwise and add to the salad bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Grate all of the zest from the lemon, then juice the lemon into a small bowl (that will be used for the salad dressing) and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine and mix together ½ of the garlic (save the rest for the salad dressing), lemon zest, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pat dry the lamb chops with paper towels and place on a plate; rub both sides of the chops with the spice mixture.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the lamb chops in the skillet; cook until they are nicely seared and cooked to your desired doneness, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer the chops to a plate and let them rest for 5 minutes.
While the lamb chops cook, scoop out the avocado flesh into the bowl with the lemon juice and mash with a fork until smooth.
To make the dressing, add the remaining garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper to the avocado and lemon mixture; mix together.
To serve, arrange the salad on a plate, spoon the avocado dressing overtop, and place the lamb chops on the side. Enjoy!

name: Pan Seared Pork Chops with Crispy Vietnamese Cabbage & Mint Salad

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork chops and sear until golden and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from heat and transfer to a clean plate. Cover loosely with aluminum foil and set aside.
Meanwhile, place edamame in a colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain.
Juice lime into a medium bowl.
Add fish sauce, oil, sugar, and, chili-garlic sauce to the bowl with the lime juice; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice the shallot into half-moons; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; halve the cabbage lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise into shreds. Add to the bowl.
Trim cucumber, halve lengthwise, and thinly slice crosswise; add to the bowl.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl along with the edamame and toss to combine the salad.
Thinly slice pork chops.
To serve, divide salad and pork chops between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Sautéed Apples & Roasted Green Beans

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F and position the rack in the centre.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and discard the ends of the green beans; transfer the beans to a baking sheet pan.
Drizzle the green beans with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then spread them out in a single layer.
Place the beans in the oven and roasted while you prepare the pork chops, 5 to 7 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
One by one, holding a sprig of thyme at its top, run you fingers down it to remove the leaves. Discard the sprigs and chop the leaves. Transfer the thyme to a small bowl.
In a small bowl, combine and mix together salt, pepper, and ½ of the thyme (save the rest for the apples).
Place the pork chops on a plate and rub both sides with the spice mixture.
Once the skillet is heated, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they are golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes per side.

While the pork chops cook, remove the green beans from the oven and make room for the pork chops in the middle. Once the chops are seared, transfer them to the baking sheet and remove the skillet from the heat.
Return the baking sheet to the oven; cook until the pork chops are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife) and the green beans are tender-crisp, 6 to 10 minutes.
Quarter the apple lengthwise, then cut out the core and stem from each section; cut each quarter lengthwise into 4 thin wedges.
Return the skillet to the stove over medium heat.
Add coconut oil, apples, and the remaining thyme to the skillet; season with salt and pepper. Cook the apples, stirring occasionally, until they are tender and lightly browned, 4 to 6 minutes.
To serve, place the pork chops and green beans on a plate and spoon the sautéed apples on top of the pork. Enjoy!

name: Pan Seared Ribeye with Steak Sauce & Broccoli-Asparagus Sauté

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, cut the steak into portions, pat dry with paper towels, and place on a plate; season with spices on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus; cut spears into 2-inch pieces and add to the bowl with the broccoli.
When the steak is done, return the skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until fork-tender, 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, place ketchup, Dijon, Worcestershire, vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and crushed red pepper in a small bowl; whisk to combine the steak sauce and set aside.
When the veggies are done, juice lemon into the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide steak and veggies between plates; drizzle sauce over steaks and enjoy!

name: Pan Seared Salmon with Soy Tossed Mushrooms & Zucchini-Thyme Rice

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim off the root end and dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut the leek in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces and place in a small bowl.
Trim and small dice zucchini; add to the bowl with the leek.
Slide thyme leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Add leaves to the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, place rice in a strainer or colander and rinse under cold, running water.

Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add veggies and rice. Cook, stirring constantly, until the veggies start to soften, 2-3 minutes. Stir in broth and salt, then bring to a boil over high heat.
amounts: 8 fl oz (1 cup) chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Once the liquid in the saucepan comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook until the liquid is mostly absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat salmon dry with paper towels and place skin-side down on a plate; season the top side with salt and pepper.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add salmon, skin-side down, and cook, flipping once, until skin is crispy and flesh is opaque, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use).
Meanwhile, thinly slice mushrooms. Peel and mince garlic.
Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium-high heat; add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add mushrooms and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Add soy sauce to the skillet and continue to cook until the liquid has evaporated, 1-2 minutes more; remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice between plates or bowls; top with salmon and mushrooms. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Warmed Potato, Corn & Snap Pea Salad

ingredients.name: sugar snap peas
ingredients.display: ½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
amounts: ½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas

instructions.text: Medium dice the potatoes (cut into ¾-inch cubes) and transfer to a baking sheet.
Add the corn to the potatoes.
Drizzle the potatoes and corn with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then arrange in a single layer.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Place the sheet in the oven and roast until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork, 18 to 20 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a medium bowl (that is big enough to hold the potato salad).
Add mayonnaise, paprika, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the garlic and mix together.
Cut the sugar snap peas crosswise (at an angle) into ¼-inch pieces and transfer to the salad bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat dry the salmon with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is warm, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Place the salmon, skin-side down, in the skillet; cook until it is cooked through and flaky, 3 to 5 minutes per side (depending on thickness). Once done, transfer the salmon to a plate.
While the salmon cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise (at an angle) into ¼-inch pieces and transfer to the salad bowl.
Once the potatoes are tender, remove them from the oven and transfer to the salad bowl. Mix the ingredients together.
To serve, spoon the salad onto a plate and place the salmon on top. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Scallops with Avocado-Orange Salsa & Quinoa

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine the quinoa, salt, and water; bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the quinoa for 15 minutes. Once done, remove the quinoa from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.

Cut off a piece from each stem end of the oranges to reveal the flesh, slice off the skin and pith, then cut the oranges lengthwise into 8 wedges. Cut the wedges crosswise into small pieces and transfer to a medium bowl (that will hold the salsa).
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and medium dice the flesh. Add to the salsa bowl.

Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add ½ of the cilantro to the salsa bowl and transfer the other ½ to a small bowl (for the quinoa).
Trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and mince the shallot. Add to the salsa bowl.
Juice the lime and add to the salsa bowl.
Drizzle the salsa with olive oil and season with crushed red pepper, salt, and pepper; toss to combine.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the scallops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper on both sides.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Once the skillet is hot, carefully add the scallops in a single layer; cook until they develop a nice sear and are opaque throughout, 1 ½ to 2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Uncover the quinoa, add the remaining cilantro, and fluff with a fork.
To serve, divide the quinoa between plates; top with the salsa and then the scallops. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Scallops with Pea Purée & Grapefruit-Arugula Salad

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); bring to a boil over high heat.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.
In a large salad bowl, combine and whisk together olive oil, vinegar, honey, Dijon, salt, and pepper.

Slice off a piece from both grapefruit ends, then place it flat on one of the ends and slice off the peel (from top to bottom), exposing the flesh; cut out the segments of flesh from between the membranes. Add to the salad bowl.
Add the arugula to the salad bowl and toss until the salad is thoroughly coated with the dressing.

Once the water is boiling, season with salt and add the peas. Cook until the peas are bright green and tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain the peas in a colander, reserving ½ cup of the cooking water, and return to the saucepan.
Add the butter, garlic, and reserved cooking water to the peas. Using a hand blender, purée the mixture until smooth. Alternatively, use a potato masher to mash the peas.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the scallops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper on both sides.
amounts: ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: Once the skillet is hot, carefully add the scallops in a single layer; cook until they develop a nice sear and are opaque throughout, 1 ½ to 2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
To serve, divide the pea purée between plates, then top with the salad and scallops. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Scallops with Tomato-Basil Linguine

instructions.text: Fill a large pot halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the scallops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; rub with oil and season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, carefully add the scallops in a single layer; cook until they develop a nice sear and are opaque throughout, 1½-2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice the onion.
Return skillet to medium heat, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 4 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic.
Add tomatoes, garlic, and crushed red pepper to the skillet with the onions; stir to combine. Bring to a boil over high heat then reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash basil, pick leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Add scallops, capers, and basil to the sauce; simmer 1 minute more.
Drain pasta, add to the skillet, and toss to coat.
To serve, divide pasta, sauce, and scallops between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Steak with Sautéed Brussels Sprouts

instructions.text: Wash sprouts, trim rough ends and halve lengthwise. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Season steak generously with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Place steak in skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil; set aside.
Peel and thinly slice shallot. Peel and mince garlic.
Once steak has been transferred, melt butter in skillet. Add brussels sprouts, shallot, and garlic. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sprouts are browned, 4-5 minutes.
Add ½ cup water to sprouts and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sprouts are tender and liquid has evaporated, 4-5 minutes.
Drizzle with vinegar and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for another 1-2 minutes.
Serve steak with brussels sprouts on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Seared Strip Steak with Kale Colcannon (Irish Mashed Potatoes)

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

ingredients.name: striploin (new york strip) steak
ingredients.display: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and quarter the potatoes; transfer to a small saucepan.
Cover the potatoes with hot water (from the tap); bring to a boil over high heat.
Cut out and discard the center stems from the kale leaves; slice the leaves crosswise into ⅛-inch strips and transfer to a medium bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat dry the steak with paper towels and place on a plate. Season the steak generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
amounts: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.text: Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce the heat to medium and cook until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife, 15 to 20 minutes. Once done, drain the potatoes and return to the saucepan; cover to keep warm.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
While the steak cooks, trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Once the steak has been transferred, reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and kale; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the kale is wilted, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add butter, broth, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher until smooth.
amounts: 4 fl oz (½ cup) chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Add the kale to the saucepan and mash with the potatoes.
To serve, divide the colcannon and steak between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan Seared Tilapia with Corn-Peach Salad & Couscous

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, remove from heat, add couscous, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork.
amounts: 8 fl oz (1 cup) chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place oil, vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve grape tomatoes. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter peaches lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pits. Medium dice the flesh and add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion. Add to the bowl.
Place corn in the colander and rinse under hot water (from the tap) to thaw. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the salad, and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with spices on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the tilapia and cook, flipping once, until fish is crispy and easily flakes with a fork, about 6 minutes. Remove from heat.
Divide tilapia and couscous between plates; top tilapia with a small portion of salad. Serve with remaining salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Panko-Crusted Fish Sticks with Lemon-Herb Dip & Carrot-Apple Slaw

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 450°F and place the rack in the center position.
Crack the egg into a shallow bowl and season with salt and pepper, then beat with a whisk or fork.
On a large plate, combine bread crumbs and olive oil; mix together.
Slice the fish fillets crosswise into ½-inch-wide strips.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or foil.
Working in batches, dip the fish in the egg mixture (allowing excess to drip back into bowl), then coat with the bread crumbs (pressing gently to help them adhere); transfer to the baking sheet.
Place the fish sticks in the oven and bake until the bread crumbs are golden brown and the fish is opaque in the middle, 15 to 18 minutes.
While the fish cooks, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the apple, then cut out the core and stem from each section. Using a box grater, coarsely grate the apple sections and transfer to a medium salad bowl.
Peel the carrots, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Using a box grater, coarsely grate the carrots and add to the salad bowl.

Using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Transfer ½ of the parsley to the salad bowl and the other ½ to a medium bowl (that will be used for the dip and salad dressing).
Measure out the raisins and add to the salad bowl.
Juice the lemon and pour into the medium bowl with the parsley.
Add mayo, yogurt, Dijon, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the parsley and lemon juice; whisk together.
Reserve half of the sauce as a dip for the fish sticks and transfer the rest to the salad bowl; toss the salad to coat.
To serve, place the fish sticks and slaw on a plate and serve with the remaining dip. Enjoy!

name: Panko Crusted Tilapia with Lemon Parmesan Asparagus

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Finely grate the Parmesan.
Snap (or cut) off the woody ends of the asparagus. Transfer to a baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil, season with the salt and pepper, and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake for 15 minutes.
While the asparagus cooks, pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and place on a plate.
In a medium bowl, add the flour.
In a second bowl, add the egg and water; whisk until smooth.
In a third bowl, add the bread crumbs and salt. Stir to combine.
To coat the tilapia, dip each fillet into the flour, then the egg, and finally the bread crumbs. Press gently to adhere.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the fish to the skillet and cook until golden brown on each side, 3-4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Once the asparagus is done, juice the lemon and pour the lemon juice over the asparagus.
To serve, divide the fish and asparagus between plates. Enjoy!

name: Paprika Chicken Drumsticks with Spicy Carrot, Mint & Cashew Salad

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and place in a medium bowl. Drizzle with oil, season with spices, and toss to coat. Transfer chicken to the baking sheet, spreading it out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, turning halfway through, until chicken is golden and cooked through, 25-30 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic. Place in a clean medium bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add oil, Dijon, and spices, then whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrots. Add to the bowl with the dressing.

Halve jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Slice crosswise into thin half-moons and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop cashews. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chicken and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Paprika Pork Chop with Bacon, Zucchini & Tomato Sauté

instructions.text: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, medium dice bacon.

Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 3-4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove crispy bacon to a paper towel-lined plate, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
While the bacon is cooking, pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on another plate; season with spices on both sides.

When the bacon is done, return skillet (with drippings) to medium-high heat. Add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry zucchini. Using a clean cutting board, trim and halve zucchini lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick half-moons.
Wash and dry tomatoes.
Peel and mince garlic.

Return skillet (with cooking juices) to medium-high heat; add zucchini, tomatoes, garlic, and spices. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is tender and tomatoes start to burst, 6-7 minutes.
When the veggies are done, add water and continue to cook until the sauce has thickened, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide chops, veggies, and sauce between plates; sprinkle with crispy bacon and enjoy!

name: Paprika Pork Chop, Balsamic Mushrooms & Wilted Spinach with Parmesan

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Add vinegar, oil, maple syrup, soy sauce, salt, and thyme to the bowl with the garlic; whisk to combine the sauce.

Quarter mushrooms, add to the bowl, and toss to coat; transfer to the baking sheet and spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven and roast, stirring halfway through, until tender and caramelized, about 15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with spices on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
While the chops are cooking, finely grate Parmesan and set aside.
Peel and mince additional garlic. Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces.
When the chops are done, wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and green onions; cook, stirring constantly, until soft and fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Add Parmesan and salt, stir to combine, and remove from the heat.
To serve, divide pork chops, mushrooms, and spinach between plates. Enjoy!

name: Paprika Pork Chops with Sautéed Bell Pepper, Mango & Red Onion

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the bell pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Slice the quarters crosswise into small strips and transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; cut lengthwise into thin wedges. Add to the bowl with the bell pepper.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with paprika, salt, and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they develop a nice crust, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and cook the chops, flipping occasionally, until they are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife), another 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer the pork to a plate.
While the pork chops cook, peel the mango, then slice off the flesh from the pit, starting with the flatter sides; discard the pit and large dice the flesh (cut into ¾-inch cubes).
Once the pork chops have been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet.
Add the bell pepper and onion to the skillet; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are just tender, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the mango to the skillet; stir to combine and continue cooking for an additional 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from the heat.
To serve, divide the pork chops and sauté between plates. Enjoy!

name: Paprika Pork Chops with Yogurt-Dressed Waldorf Salad

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Place pork chops in a small baking dish. Rub both sides with paprika, salt, and pepper.
Place in the oven and bake until cooked through, 15-20 minutes.
In a medium bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together lemon juice, yogurt, honey, salt, and pepper.
Wash and dry apples and celery. Core and medium dice apples. Medium dice celery. Add to bowl with dressing.
Add raisins to bowl. Roughly chop walnuts and add to bowl. Toss salad.
Cut remaining piece of lemon into wedges for serving.
To serve, place pork chops and salad on a plate and garnish with lemon wedges. Enjoy!

name: Paprika Pork Stew (Goulash) with Bell Pepper, Tomato & Dill Potatoes

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Place potatoes in a medium saucepan, cover with hot water (from the tap), and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer until potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork, 10-12 minutes. Drain and return to the saucepan; cover to keep warm.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrots; add to the bowl with the onion and garlic.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Preheat another medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels, then cut into 2-inch cubes; season with salt and pepper.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add pork and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 3-4 minutes (the pork will not be cooked all the way through).
Add veggies to the pan with the pork and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies soften, 3-4 minutes.

Add tomatoes and spices to the pan; stir to combine and bring the stew to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender and pork is cooked through, 8-10 minutes.

Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the pan with the potatoes along with oil and salt; lightly crush with a fork or potato masher and cover to keep warm. (Reserve remaining dill for the stew.)
When the stew is done, add reserved dill to the pan, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide potatoes and pork stew between plates or bowls; top with yogurt and enjoy!

name: Paprika Salmon with Grilled Eggplant & Basil Vinaigrette

instructions.text: Heat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together oil, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Rub salmon with spice mixture.
Coat grill or bottom of skillet with oil. Add salmon and cook until opaque, 4-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Wash, dry, and slice eggplant into ¼ inch thick pieces. Transfer to a large bowl, drizzle with oil, and season with salt; toss to coat.
Add eggplant to grill/skillet and cook until tender and lightly browned, 2-3 minutes per side.
Wash and dry basil. Pick leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Peel and mince garlic. In a small bowl, whisk together basil, garlic, oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
To serve, place salmon and eggplant on a plate and drizzle with basil vinaigrette. Enjoy!

name: Parmesan Cauliflower Rice with Ground Beef, Mushrooms & Spinach

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Cut cauliflower head into quarters; using a box grater, hold the stem end of the cauliflower and coarsely grate. (Alternatively, transfer cauliflower to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until rice-like in consistency.) Place in a medium bowl.
Thinly slice mushrooms. Add to the bowl with the cauliflower rice along with oil and spices, then stir to combine. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until cauliflower and mushrooms are tender and golden, 18-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add beef, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
While the beef is cooking, finely grate Parmesan. Set aside.
When the beef is done, add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Stir to combine, remove from heat, and cover to keep warm.
When the cauliflower rice and mushrooms are done, remove from oven. Carefully add both to the skillet with the beef mixture along with Parmesan and soy sauce. Stir to combine.
To serve, divide cauliflower rice between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Parmesan-Chili Butter Gnocchi with Basil & Mushroom-Spinach Salad

instructions.text: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Place half in a medium bowl along with mayo, vinegar, water, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
Thinly slice mushrooms. Add to the bowl with the dressing and set aside.
Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
While the water heats up, finely grate Parmesan. Set aside.
Once the water in the pan is boiling, add gnocchi and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until gnocchi begins to float to the surface, about 3 minutes. Drain in a colander and set aside.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chili-garlic sauce and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add drained gnocchi and Parmesan to the skillet with the chili butter. Continue to cook, stirring often, until cheese is melted and gnocchi are coated in sauce, 1 minute more. Remove from heat.
Add spinach to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide gnocchi and salad between plates or bowls. Top gnocchi with reserved basil and enjoy!

name: Parmesan-Panko Crusted Pork Cutlets with Squash, Apple & Arugula Salad

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)

Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out seeds, and medium dice the flesh. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until squash is golden brown and fork-tender, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Transfer to a plate along with bread crumbs and spices. Stir to combine the coating and set aside.
Place egg in a medium bowl and beat with a whisk or fork until smooth. Set aside.
Pat pork dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chops in half horizontally to form thin cutlets.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, dip the cutlets into the beaten egg (letting the excess drip off), then into the bread crumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere. Transfer to another plate.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the breaded cutlets and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper in a clean medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Using a clean cutting board, quarter, core, and medium dice apple. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Add cooled squash and arugula to the bowl. Toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide pork cutlets and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Parmesan & Parsley Crusted Chicken with Roasted Romaine Lettuce

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.display: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Slice chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with salt and pepper. Place on a baking sheet pan.
amounts: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless

instructions.text: Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Grate ¼ cup of Parmesan cheese. Peel and mince garlic.
In a small bowl, combine parsley, Parmesan, garlic, bread crumbs, and olive oil. Mix well and pat onto chicken fillets.
Place chicken in the oven and bake while you prepare the romaine, about 5 minutes.
Wash and dry lettuce. Quarter lengthwise. Place on sheet with chicken and season with salt and pepper.
Return sheet to the oven and roast until chicken is cooked through and romaine is browned at the edges, another 5-10 minutes.
Cut ½ lemon into wedges.
To serve, place chicken and romaine hearts on a plate. Garnish with lemon wedges and sprinkle romaine hearts with pine nuts. Enjoy!

name: Parmesan Polenta with Garlicky Shrimp, Spinach, Tomatoes, Corn & Basil

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen raw peeled shrimp
ingredients.display: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, bring water to a boil. Reduce heat to low and gradually add polenta in a thin steady stream, while whisking, until the polenta is incorporated; add salt. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until polenta is soft and the texture is creamy, 15-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and thinly slice garlic. Place in a small bowl and set aside.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tomatoes and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are beginning to burst, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Place half in a medium bowl along with the spinach. (Set remaining basil aside for serving.)

If using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
amounts: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen

instructions.text: When the tomatoes are done, add to the bowl with the garlic. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp, salt, and crushed red pepper; cook until just opaque and starting to color, 1 minute per side.
When the shrimp are done, add garlic and tomatoes to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until garlic is fragrant, 1-2 minutes more.
Add spinach and basil to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Remove shrimp sauté from heat, juice lemon into the skillet, and stir to combine. Cover to keep warm and set aside.
Finely grate Parmesan.

When the polenta is done, add Parmesan, corn, oil, and pepper to the pan; stir to combine. Continue to cook until corn is warmed through, 1-2 minutes more; if the polenta is too firm, add hot water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until you reach a desired consistency. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide polenta between plates or bowls; top with shrimp-tomato sauté and reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Parmesan Polenta with Lemony Kale-Corn Sauté & Fried Egg

ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.display: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Reduce heat to low and gradually add polenta in a thin steady stream, while whisking, until the polenta is incorporated; add salt. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until polenta is soft and the texture is creamy, 15-25 minutes.
amounts: 24 fl oz (3 cups) chicken or vegetable broth
